issues.description: DESIGN SPEC for §5.15 Phase B — 10 Codex Local-exec/engineering tool renderers. Each tool needs (a) inline conversation card, (b) right-side detail panel, sharing the same primitives as Claude Code's existing renderers and the §5.18 compact-inline / verbose-sidebar pattern.
issues.location: packages/happy-app/sources/components/tools/knownTools.tsx (registration); packages/happy-app/sources/components/tools/views/ (new view components for tools that need richer-than-default rendering)
issues.details:
Phase B covers 10 Codex `functions.*` tools. `functions.exec_command` is already wired through CodexBashView (DONE). For the remaining 9, the design pattern is the same registration shape used by §5.15 Phase A (10 web tools at knownTools.tsx:955-1099):

```ts
'<tool_name>': {
  title: t('tools.names.<key>'),
  icon: ICON_<CATEGORY>,
  minimal: true,
  input: z.object({...}).partial().passthrough(),
  result: z.object({...}).partial().passthrough(),
  extractDescription: ({ tool }) => <one-line summary string>,
}
```

The inline card is rendered by ToolView (default) which uses ToolHeader + ToolStatusIndicator. The right-side sidebar uses ToolFullView which routes to a dedicated *ViewFull.tsx OR falls back to the generic Description/Input/Output layout (CronList post-§5.18). Tools that need richer Output rendering need a custom view.

PER-TOOL DESIGN BRIEFS:

1. `apply_patch` — closes §5.14 (multi-file edit no right-sidebar). Already has CodexPatchView.tsx (175 lines, ToolDiffView per file). Inline card: ICON_EDIT (file-diff) + 'Edit N files: a.ts, b.ts, …' (extractDescription summarizes count + first 2 file names). Sidebar: re-use CodexPatchView per-file diffs grouped under 'Output' section. Description = real model description (not raw command — fixes §5.7 regression for this tool). Mobile: per-file diff blocks already use ToolSectionView fullWidth + horizontal scroll on long lines.

2. `write_stdin` — interactive process input. Inline card: ICON_TERMINAL + 'Send to PID <id>: <text-preview>' (truncate input.text to 60 chars). Sidebar Output: monospace block showing the text sent + acknowledgement from process. Status indicator follows `state` (running/completed/error). Mobile: identical, single-column.

3. `update_plan` — task plan tracking. Inline card: ICON_TODO (bulb) + 'Plan: N items (M completed)' (count from input.steps). Sidebar Output: vertical list of plan items each with a status chip (pending/in_progress/completed) — re-use the TodoView visual primitive (ItemList + status pill). Mobile: same vertical list, full-width.

4. `request_user_input` — user prompt. Inline card: ICON_QUESTION (help-circle-outline) + 'Ask: <header truncated to 60 chars>'. Use the existing AskUserQuestionView.tsx as Output renderer (already supports questions[].header + options[]). Mobile: each question stacks vertically, options become full-width pressable rows.

5. `list_mcp_resources` — directory of MCP resources. Inline card: ICON_SEARCH + 'List MCP: <server>' (input.server name). Sidebar Output: table of [resource_uri, name, description] in a horizontally-scrollable container (re-use the §5.8 wide-table wrapper). Status: completed-with-count, e.g. 'Found 14 resources'.

6. `list_mcp_resource_templates` — same shape as above with 'List templates: <server>'. Sidebar Output table columns [template, parameters[], description]. Re-use the wide-table wrapper. 

7. `read_mcp_resource` — fetch one resource. Inline card: ICON_READ (eye) + 'Read MCP: <uri-truncated>'. Sidebar Output: text/markdown body if string; JSON tree if object. Re-use ToolSectionView for the body. Mobile: monospace text block with horizontal scroll like CodexBashView.

8. `view_image` — local image preview. Inline card: ICON_IMAGE (already used by web.image_query) + 'View image: <basename>'. Sidebar Output: <Image source={{ uri: file://<path> }}> with `style={{ width: '100%', aspectRatio: <derived> }}` and a max-height of 400. If image fails to load, show a 'broken-image' Octicon + path. Mobile: aspectRatio constrained, never overflow card width.

9. `mcp__happy__change_title` — already exists at knownTools.tsx:600 as `change_title` with hidden:true, minimal:true, noStatus:true. NO additional design needed. ACCEPTED AS-IS for Phase B (the existing entry is keyed without the `mcp__happy__` prefix; a Codex-style alias entry pointing to the same definition may be needed if the Codex stream uses the full name — Dev to confirm protocol mapping; design-side this is a one-line registration aliasing).

10. `exec_command` — DONE via CodexBashView.tsx (already in production). Listed for completeness.

ALIGNMENT WITH §5.7: For ALL 10 tools, Description in the sidebar must come from the model's natural-language description field (or a t(...)-formatted string built from input args), NEVER from the raw `input.command`/`input.text`/`input.uri` blob. The existing 10 web tools at knownTools.tsx:955-1099 are the canonical example: `extractDescription` returns a t(...)-formatted summary, not the raw input.

ALIGNMENT WITH §5.18: All inline cards must be a single line (icon + name + extractDescription summary). Verbose Description/Input/Output blocks belong in the sidebar (ToolFullView), not inline.

issues.description: DESIGN SPEC for §5.15 Phase C — 5 Codex Subagent/delegation tool renderers. Closes §5.13 (Codex subagent tasks not displayed). Mirror Claude Code's Agent (Task) tool visibility pattern.
issues.location: packages/happy-app/sources/components/tools/knownTools.tsx (5 new entries); packages/happy-app/sources/components/tools/views/CodexSubagentView.tsx (new) — recommend ONE shared view component covering all 5 lifecycle verbs.
issues.details:
Phase C covers 5 Codex `functions.*` tools that form one logical 'subagent lifecycle' group: spawn_agent → send_input → wait_agent → resume_agent → close_agent. Design as a single visual family.

SHARED ICON: ICON_TASK (Octicons rocket, already used by Claude Code's Agent tool at knownTools.tsx:11). Subagent name/description in inline card and sidebar.

PER-TOOL INLINE CARD:

1. `spawn_agent` — ICON_TASK + 'Spawn: <agent_name>' (or '<agent_name>: <prompt-truncated>' if input.prompt present). Status: running spinner during spawn, completed checkmark when agent registered.

2. `send_input` — ICON_TASK + 'Send to <agent_name>: <input-truncated to 60 chars>'. Status follows lifecycle.

3. `wait_agent` — ICON_TASK + 'Wait for <agent_name> (<timeout>s)'. While running: spinner with 'waiting…' label.

4. `resume_agent` — ICON_TASK + 'Resume: <agent_name>'. Status: completed once resumed.

5. `close_agent` — ICON_TASK + 'Close: <agent_name>'. Status: completed (one-shot).

SIDEBAR (Right Detail Panel):

Re-use TaskView.tsx (lines 33-54, 178 lines total) which renders:
- Subagent name in header
- Description text
- TaskStatusRow with up to 3 visible tools + 'and N more' (lines 41-42, 110-115)
- Each tool item is pressable (onSubToolPress) to drill into the tool's own detail

ADAPTATION FOR CODEX:
- For spawn_agent: header = agent_name, description = system prompt or task brief, TaskStatusRow shows the agent's first 3 tool calls (resolved from messages[] filtered by agent_id).
- For send_input/wait_agent/resume_agent/close_agent: NO TaskStatusRow needed (these are control-plane events, not subagent containers). Sidebar shows just Description + Input Parameters + Output (e.g. wait_agent Output = 'Agent completed in 28s' + final state).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA mapping:
- §5.15 acceptance point 6 'spawn_agent / wait_agent / resume_agent / close_agent rendering is what resolves §5.13' — satisfied by registering all 5 entries with ICON_TASK + extractDescription.
- §5.7 (Description not raw args) — extractDescription uses agent_name + truncated prompt, NEVER the raw JSON input blob.

MOBILE: TaskView.tsx is already mobile-friendly (line 41 `visibleTools.slice(filtered.length - 3)` caps at 3 items; line 162 `flex: 1` on toolTitle handles narrow viewports). Single-column on 390px viewport.
issues.observation_notes:
Reference: TaskView.tsx (Claude Code Agent tool renderer) is the canonical visibility pattern — header + description + status row of tool calls + status icons (running spinner / completed check / error X). The 5 Codex subagent verbs map to a subset of this pattern: spawn_agent gets the FULL TaskView treatment (because it owns child tool calls), the other 4 (send_input/wait_agent/resume_agent/close_agent) get a degenerate version (no TaskStatusRow).

A single new view component CodexSubagentView.tsx (~80 lines, reuses TaskStatusRow + ToolStatusIcon imports from TaskView.tsx) is sufficient. Adding 5 entries to knownTools.tsx (each ~12 lines) = ~140 LOC total for Phase C.
issues.evidence: TaskView.tsx (Claude Code reference); e2e-desktop-1440x900-session.png shows 'PM PLAN: build test plan from spec' + 'UI specialist: design Codex tool renderers' Agent cards rendering with this exact pattern (rocket icon header + tool list + status icons). Phase C must reproduce this visibility for Codex spawn_agent.

issues.description: DESIGN SPEC for §5.15 Phase D — 2 plugin/tool-suggest renderers. Collapsible card listing constituent tool calls.
issues.details:
Phase D covers 2 tools — both have a 'meta' shape (they wrap or refer to other tool calls).

1. `tool_suggest` — Codex suggests installing/enabling a plugin.
   - Inline card: ICON_REASONING (light-bulb, knownTools.tsx:19) + 'Suggest: <plugin_name>'. extractDescription truncates input.plugin or input.suggestion.
   - Sidebar: Description (suggestion text), Input Parameters (plugin metadata), Output (model's rationale string).
   - Status: noStatus: true (this is informational, no async lifecycle).
   - Re-use the generic ToolFullView with no custom view component (the default Description/Input/Output rendering is sufficient).

2. `multi_tool_use.parallel` — Codex runs N tool calls in parallel. The card lists each constituent tool call with its own status icon.
   - Inline card: ICON_TASK + 'Parallel: <N> tools' (extractDescription counts input.tool_uses.length).
   - Sidebar (CodexParallelView): each constituent tool call rendered as a pressable row with [icon | tool name | one-line summary | status icon]. Tapping a row drills into that child tool's detail (re-use the same onSubToolPress prop pattern from TaskView.tsx:34, 49, 87).
   - Visual style: COPY TaskStatusRow exactly (TaskView.tsx:97-121). The only difference: 'Parallel' is the header label, not a subagent name.

ACCEPTANCE: §5.15 acceptance point 5 'Codex tool rendering layer must share the same redesigned popup / card primitives used by Claude Code'. Phase D adds zero new visual primitives — both renderers are pure compositions of existing ones.

MOBILE: Same handling as TaskView (already mobile-friendly).
issues.observation_notes:
Phase D is the smallest of the three phases (~50 LOC). The hardest part is the protocol-side parsing of `multi_tool_use.parallel`: input.tool_uses is an array of {tool_name, args} entries, and each must be projected into a synthetic ToolCall shape so existing renderers can be re-used. That's a sessionProtocolMapper.ts concern, not a UI design concern — flagged here only as awareness.

TaskStatusRow (TaskView.tsx:97-121) is the canonical pattern: View > View > [ToolItemRow * N] > Text 'and N more'. Each ToolItemRow has flex-1 toolTitle + auto-margin statusContainer = perfectly mobile-responsive.
issues.evidence: TaskView.tsx:97-121 (TaskStatusRow primitive); e2e-mobile-390x844-session.png shows TaskStatusRow rendering 3 tool items + '+26 more tools' on a 390px viewport without overflow.

issues.description: CANONICAL DESIGN RECIPE established by §5.18 (CronList simplification) — applies uniformly to ALL Phase B/C/D tool renderers. This is a meta-finding documenting the contract dev should follow when implementing Phases B/C/D.
issues.details:
INLINE CARD CONTRACT (compact):
- One row only: <icon> <tool_name> <one-line extractDescription summary>
- NO inline INPUT block
- NO inline OUTPUT block
- Status indicator (right-aligned) following the existing pattern: ActivityIndicator (running) / checkmark (completed) / X (error)
- Tappable / pressable to open the detail panel

SIDEBAR (verbose) CONTRACT:
- Three top-level sections, each with its own colored icon header (per qa-blk2-cronlist-desktop-sidebar.png):
  1. Description (info-circle icon, purple) — REAL natural-language description, NEVER raw args (§5.7).
  2. Input Parameters (bracket icon, navy) — structured display of the input object.
  3. Output (folder icon, green) — rendered per tool type (text monospace / image / diff / table / list).
- Each section uses ToolSectionView (fullWidth on mobile).
- Mobile: vertical stack, full-width. Desktop: same vertical stack, max-width capped by ToolFullView container.

DIFFERENTIATION TABLE (when to use a custom view vs the default):

| Tool | Custom View Needed? | Why |
|------|---|---|
| apply_patch | YES (CodexPatchView.tsx exists) | per-file diff rendering |
| view_image | YES | <Image> rendering |
| update_plan | YES | TodoView-style list with status chips |
| request_user_input | YES (AskUserQuestionView.tsx exists) | clickable options |
| list_mcp_resources | YES | wide-table with horizontal scroll |
| list_mcp_resource_templates | YES | wide-table |
| read_mcp_resource | OPTIONAL | text/markdown body — default Output may suffice |
| write_stdin | NO | default monospace Output is fine |
| exec_command | YES (CodexBashView.tsx exists, DONE) | command + multi-line stdout/stderr |
| change_title | NO (already hidden:true) | not user-visible |
| spawn_agent | YES (new CodexSubagentView.tsx) | TaskStatusRow with child tool calls |
| send_input/wait_agent/resume_agent/close_agent | NO | default Description/Input/Output sufficient |
| tool_suggest | NO | default sufficient |
| multi_tool_use.parallel | YES (new CodexParallelView.tsx) | TaskStatusRow with parallel tool calls |

Net new view components needed: 5 (CodexSubagentView, CodexParallelView, CodexUpdatePlanView, CodexViewImageView, CodexMcpListView — last one shared by list_mcp_resources + list_mcp_resource_templates). Plus 12 entries in knownTools.tsx.
issues.observation_notes: The §5.18 sidebar reference screenshot (qa-blk2-cronlist-desktop-sidebar.png) is the visual ground truth: 'Description' (with colored icon) → text 'CronList call' → 'Input Parameters' (with colored icon) → JSON `{}` block → 'Output' (with colored icon) → 'No scheduled jobs.' text. This three-section layout is what every Phase B/C/D detail panel must inherit.

design_enhancements.title: Phase B/C/D detail-panel: standardize section icons + colors across all 17 new tools
design_enhancements.current_state: Only CronList and a few existing tools currently render the canonical Description/Input Parameters/Output triplet (qa-blk2-cronlist-desktop-sidebar.png shows colored circle icons: purple info, navy bracket, green folder).
design_enhancements.proposed_state: Every Phase B/C/D detail panel uses the IDENTICAL section icon set: purple info-circle for Description, navy/blue bracket for Input Parameters, green folder for Output. No per-tool variation. This creates instant visual learnability — once a user knows the three sections of one Codex tool, they know all 17.
design_enhancements.rationale: Visual consistency (Gestalt similarity) is the strongest learnability lever for a tool catalog. Diverging icon choices per tool would force users to re-learn the panel's structure for each tool.

design_enhancements.title: Phase B view_image: cap image height to 400px, show file-size below

design_enhancements.rationale: Hard-capping image height prevents a 4000px-tall photo from blowing out the sidebar. Showing dimensions + size answers 'is this the image I expected?' without an extra click.

design_enhancements.title: Phase C subagent: show subagent runtime + tokens in the inline card subtitle
design_enhancements.current_state: No subagent renderer exists yet (Phase C work). Claude Code Agent renderers (TaskView) currently show '<seconds>s' next to the spinner (visible in e2e-desktop-1440x900-session.png as '107.0s', '127.0s').
design_enhancements.proposed_state: Phase C inline cards (spawn_agent in particular) should mirror this pattern — runtime in seconds next to the status indicator. If token usage is plumbed through, additionally show '· <kt>k tokens' in textSecondary.
design_enhancements.rationale: Subagents are slow operations; users want to know they're progressing. The runtime counter is the canonical progress signal.
design_enhancements.evidence: e2e-desktop-1440x900-session.png (current Claude Code Agent runtime indicator)

design_enhancements.title: Phase D multi_tool_use.parallel: visualize parallelism with a 'lane' indicator
design_enhancements.current_state: No multi_tool_use.parallel renderer exists yet (Phase D work). Default plan = list constituent tool calls vertically (TaskStatusRow style).
design_enhancements.proposed_state: Add a 1px vertical accent bar on the LEFT of each constituent tool row (theme.colors.accent at 30% opacity), grouping them visually as 'siblings of the same parallel call'. This communicates parallelism without text.
design_enhancements.rationale: Vertical accent bars are a low-cost Gestalt-grouping cue. A user glancing at the conversation should be able to instantly see 'these 3 tool calls all ran in parallel' vs 'these 3 ran serially'.
